drafts.title: Keep the car’s smooth, engaging and confidence-inspiring driving feel
drafts.description: Customers experience a smooth, responsive and confidence-inspiring driving character: composed handling, comfortable ride and rewarding throttle/gearbox interaction that makes everyday driving and longer trips enjoyable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a blinded customer drive panel (n≥50) using a standardized mixed urban/highway loop, ≥85% of drivers rate overall driving enjoyment ≥8/10 and ≥90% rate steering/handling as 'confident' or better.
assumptions: Customer panel scoring methods and current model baseline scores are available for comparison.
Chassis tuning and NVH improvements possible within successor packaging and cost targets.
uncertainties: Subjective driving enjoyment can vary by driver preference and trim; some drivers prefer firmer sport setups.

drafts.title: Deliver consistent, punchy acceleration and smooth transmission behaviour
drafts.description: Customers feel immediate, predictable engine/torque delivery with no torque steer or hesitation, and gearbox shifts that feel smooth and sure across everyday driving conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In objective bench and on-road tests: drivetrain response time from stomping throttle to measured increase in wheel torque ≤300 ms; 0–100 km/h for the standard petrol/plug‑hybrid variant ≤8.5 s (or matching customer expectations for that power class). In a customer drive test (n≥50) ≥90% report 'no noticeable torque lag' and 'no torque steer' during normal accelerations.
assumptions: Target 0–100 km/h of ≤8.5 s is appropriate for the mainstream engine variant in this segment in 3–5 years.
Measured drivetrain response time target (≤300 ms) is achievable through calibration and transmission control improvements.
uncertainties: Exact 0–100 km/h target may vary by market and final powertrain choices; electrified variants will have inherently faster response.
Some perceived jerks may originate from tyre or suspension interactions, not the gearbox alone.

drafts.title: Provide dedicated physical controls for heating, defog and other essential functions to reduce distraction
drafts.description: Customers can change temperature, fan, defog and seat heating quickly without looking at the centre screen — basic climate and safety-related controls are available as tactile buttons/knobs and reachable by touch.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Usability test: 95% of drivers can locate and change driver temperature, fan, defog and heated-seat settings within 2 seconds while driving (eyes off road). Physical controls for these functions are present on every trim.
assumptions: Physical controls can be integrated while keeping a modern center screen and without removing desirable display functionality.
Customers value a hybrid HMI combining tactile shortcuts and a touchscreen.
uncertainties: Exact set of functions that must be physical will need validation across markets and trims.

drafts.title: Ensure infotainment and driver-assistance software is stable, intuitive and remains reliable after updates
drafts.description: Customers experience an infotainment and driver-aid system that is clear to use, rarely crashes, and retains advertised features after OTA or dealer updates — updates improve function rather than removing or degrading capabilities.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Fleet performance: after 12 months (and after at least 3 OTA releases where applied), ≤1% of vehicles report loss of core features (infotainment or driver aids). Customer-reported software complaints reduced by ≥80% versus current model within first year.
assumptions: OTA infrastructure and regression-testing processes will be in place for the successor vehicle.
Baseline current-model complaint rates are known for comparison.
uncertainties: Some faults are caused by third-party smartphone/software ecosystems outside OEM control.
Dealer support quality may continue to vary by market.

drafts.title: Deliver natural engine/acoustic character and high-fidelity cabin audio without artificial artifacts
drafts.description: Customers hear an authentic, enjoyable engine note (in relevant drive modes) and clean, high‑fidelity audio from the sound system without unnatural pops, buzzing or distortion labelled as 'fake' or unpleasant.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Objective audio lab: cabin audio system distortion (THD) ≤1% at nominal listening levels; subjective listening test: ≥80% of drivers rate the engine/audio character in 'sport' mode as 'natural' or 'very natural' and report no intrusive synthesized pops.
assumptions: Active Sound Design may still be offered but must be tuned for naturalness; lab targets for THD are achievable with current audio hardware.
Subjective engine-sound acceptability will be validated in market-representative listening panels.
uncertainties: Perception of 'natural' sound varies by customer; some prefer amplified or synthetic enhancements.

drafts.title: Seats that are comfortable, supportive and durable for long journeys
drafts.description: Customers experience seats that provide lumbar support, correct posture and long-term comfort without squeaks, poor stitching or reliability faults.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: User comfort test: ≥85% of drivers rate front-seat support ≥8/10 after a continuous 2‑hour drive. Durability: after 2,000 km real-world durability cycles, ≤2% show stitching failures, creasing beyond normal wear, or electrical seat faults.
assumptions: Durability test protocol and acceptance thresholds reflect realistic ownership patterns.
Multiple seat trim/padding options will be validated for comfort across body sizes.
uncertainties: Individual anthropometry varies; optional sporty seats may trade some long-journey comfort for lateral support.

drafts.title: Provide practical boot space and a reliable, easy-to-operate tailgate
drafts.description: Customers can carry typical everyday luggage without excessive compromise, and the tailgate opens/closes reliably and includes convenient internal controls to close the boot.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured usable boot volume ≥350 litres for combustion variants (and ≥300 litres for hybrid where battery impacts volume). Tailgate reliability: success rate ≥99% across 50 open/close cycles per vehicle sample, and an internal shut button is provided as standard.
assumptions: Targets reflect segment expectations and are achievable with successor packaging; hybrid layouts may reduce usable volume and have a separate target.
Boot volume is measured using a consistent industry-standard method.
uncertainties: Final boot volume depends on chosen powertrain architecture and spare-wheel/tire repair kit choices.

drafts.title: Offer true dual‑zone climate control with independent physical access and sufficient HVAC power
drafts.description: Customers can set separate temperatures for driver and passenger, and the system maintains the chosen temperatures with adequate cooling/heating power and accessible controls without menu dives.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Feature: independent driver/passenger temperature control is standard or clearly available; thermal performance: system keeps cabin setpoints within ±1.5°C during a standardized hot/cold cabin test. Independent controls are accessible via physical buttons/knobs or immediate shortcuts.
assumptions: HVAC sizing and packaging on successor allow for independent climate zones as standard or as a clear option.
Physical access requirement aligns with the physical-controls decision for essential functions.
uncertainties: Some entry-level trims may limit features for cost reasons; acceptance criterion assumes mainstream trim availability.

drafts.title: Reliable, open media playback and navigation that do not force mandatory app registration
drafts.description: Customers can play music from a USB stick or connected device, charge devices, and use sat-nav core functions without being forced to register or pay for app-linked features; routing and voice work dependably.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: USB audio: standard MP3/FLAC playback via USB recognized on first connection in ≥95% of attempts in test lab. Navigation: core sat‑nav routing (map guidance, turn prompts, ETA) is available and usable without mandatory app registration; voice routing accuracy ≥90% in common scenarios.
assumptions: Connectivity partners and licensing permit basic map/function availability without app binding in target markets.
USB hardware will support audio playback formats commonly used by customers.
uncertainties: Some advanced map features (live traffic, cloud POI) may still require an account or subscription in some markets.

drafts.title: Keys and driver-profile persistence that behave predictably and feel premium
drafts.description: Customers use keys (physical and digital) that feel well-built and operate reliably; the car remembers driver preferences consistently when a driver returns to the vehicle.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Digital-key and physical-key reliability: unexpected lock/unlock or alarm triggers ≤0.5% in a 12‑month field sample. Profile persistence: after unlocking and exiting/re-entering, driver profile settings are restored in ≥99% of events across 1,000 sample cycles.
assumptions: Profile persistence includes seat/mirror/climate/infotainment preferences that are stored per key or account.
Field-sample testing will include a representative set of phones and paired devices.
uncertainties: Interactions between smartphone OS updates and digital-key implementations may cause sporadic incompatibilities.

drafts.title: Progressive, predictable braking with adjustable regenerative behaviour
drafts.description: Customers experience brakes that feel linear and controllable, with regenerative braking that is smooth and configurable so stops never feel abrupt or disconnected.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Subjective test: ≥90% of drivers rate brake feel 'progressive' on combined urban and motorway loops. Functional: regenerative braking has at least three driver-selectable levels and blends seamlessly with friction brakes with no detectable sudden grab in ≥99% of braking events during test cycles.
assumptions: Electric and hybrid variants require calibrated blending; mechanical brakes must meet stopping-distance standards while still offering the required feel.
Brake feel criteria will be validated by independent test drivers.
uncertainties: Brake feel perception can be influenced by tyre choice and road surface; some trade-offs exist between regenerative strength and pedal feel.

drafts.title: Exterior mirrors that minimise blind spots and avoid distracting interior reflections
drafts.description: Customers experience clear side/rear visibility with mirrors designed to reduce blind spots and prevent interior-light reflections at night; expected mirror functions (heating, manual/power adjust) work reliably.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Visibility test: ≤5% of drivers report significant blind-spot obstruction in standardized visibility trials (day and night). Night reflection complaints ≤2% in first-year ownership surveys. Mirror heating/adjust functions operational ≥99% in reliability checks.
assumptions: Visibility trials follow a consistent test protocol with typical driver seating positions.
Mirror hardware and coatings can mitigate internal reflections within current cost/packaging constraints.
uncertainties: Some residual reflections stem from cabin lighting choices which may require guidance on user settings.

drafts.title: Tyres supplied as standard that balance low road noise with secure wet grip
drafts.description: Customers experience tyres that do not whistle excessively, remain quiet in typical use, and provide secure wet-weather grip without excessive wheelspin.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Wet braking benchmark: stopping from 80 km/h within ≤40 m on standardized wet-surface test. Exterior tyre noise on runup test ≤72 dB. First-year tyre-related customer complaints ≤2%.
assumptions: Targets align with segment-leading tyre benchmarks and can be met by selecting appropriate OE tyre compound and tread pattern.
Market-specific winter tyres are an option where required by regulation.
uncertainties: Aftermarket tyre choices and wheel size options may alter noise and grip; customer-selected larger wheels will change the delivered experience.

drafts.title: Comfortable suspension tuning that cushions poor surfaces while preserving agile handling
drafts.description: Customers experience a ride that soaks up bumps on everyday roads without compromising the composed handling that gives confidence in corners.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Combined user scoring: ≥80% of drivers rate ride comfort ≥8/10 on an urban + motorway loop with typical rough patches. Objective rough-road test shows a ≥10% reduction in vertical RMS acceleration compared with the current model baseline.
assumptions: Chassis and damper range options (adaptive/standard) will be tuned to meet both comfort and handling targets.
Baseline RMS values from current model are available for comparison.
uncertainties: Large-wheel options will reduce cushioning; target assumes standard wheel sizes on typical trims.

drafts.title: Exterior lighting that delivers clear illumination, minimal glare and robust reliability
drafts.description: Customers have bright, well-directed exterior lighting at night with minimal dazzling glare for other road users and long-term reliability of lighting hardware.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Photometric tests meet or exceed current segment standards for beam pattern and illuminance; customer lighting complaints ≤2% in first year; lighting hardware reliable ≥99% over a 3‑year simulated durability cycle.
assumptions: Photometric targets use recognized industry standards applicable in target markets.
Durability cycles simulate environmental exposure typical for EU markets.
uncertainties: Advanced adaptive lighting features may be constrained by trim level and cost.

drafts.title: Maintain the modern, high‑quality interior look and material quality
drafts.description: Customers experience a cabin that looks and feels premium with durable finishes and high perceived quality across common touchpoints.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer survey: ≥85% rate interior look and materials as 'high quality' (≥8/10) in ownership surveys after 6 months. Material durability: visible wear/tear complaints ≤2% in first year across a representative sample.
assumptions: Perceived quality is measured consistently via post-delivery surveys and dealer inspection reports.
Material and finish choices remain within premium segment expectations and regulatory constraints (e.g., recycled material policies).
uncertainties: Some customers prefer different material aesthetics; optional trims may change perception scores.

drafts.title: Improve ingress/egress and make vehicle access/exit comfortable for a wide range of customers
drafts.description: Customers can enter and exit the car comfortably without awkward bending or cramped openings — doors, seat height and grip points are designed for easy access.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: User test across a representative sample (n≥50) with varied body sizes: ≥95% can enter and exit without reporting discomfort or awkward manoeuvring. Door aperture and seat-edge height targets are validated in ergonomic tests.
assumptions: Ergonomic targets will be set against anthropometric datasets representative of EU customers.
Successor packaging (wheelbase/cabin layout) allows modest improvements in door aperture and seat positioning.
uncertainties: Trade-offs may exist between lowering the sill for ingress and maintaining sporty styling or chassis stiffness requirements.

drafts.title: Instrument cluster that is robust, easy to read and non‑distracting
drafts.description: Customers experience a digital instrument display that reliably shows critical driving information, does not crash or remove essential functions, and does not create distracting reflections under normal lighting conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cluster uptime ≥99.9% over 12 months in fleet testing. In controlled glare/reflection tests ≤5% of drivers report distracting reflections; key driving info accessible within one glance using standard display modes.
assumptions: Display hardware and anti-reflective coatings are selected to minimize reflections; software will default to high-contrast modes for night driving.
Baseline failure/uptime metrics for current model are available.
uncertainties: Reflections can be affected by aftermarket tinting, occupant clothing, and cabin lighting choices.

drafts.title: Reliable connected services and core functions that do not degrade over ownership
drafts.description: Customers have connected-services features that work reliably, are easy to set up, and remain available without frequent dealership intervention.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Connected-services availability ≥99% uptime in service windows; setup success rate for smartphone pairing and basic connected features ≥95% on first attempt in lab tests; customer complaints on connectivity reduced by ≥70% versus current model.
assumptions: Connected-services availability depends on third-party network providers; service-level monitoring will be implemented.
Onboarding flows will be simplified and tested across popular smartphone platforms.
uncertainties: Regulatory and third-party app policies may require region-specific differences in features and setup.

drafts.title: Offer a successor interior packaging that improves rear-seat spatial impression
drafts.description: Customers in the rear seats experience noticeably more legroom and a more spacious spatial impression than the current model, making rear seating more usable for adults.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Passenger trial: ≥80% of rear-seat occupants rate legroom/spatial comfort ≥7/10 on a 1.5-hour trip. Measured rear legroom increases vs current model baseline by at least one meaningful bracket (industry-standard measurement, e.g., +20–40 mm).
assumptions: Successor wheelbase and interior packaging allow incremental rear-legroom gains (as suggested by Neue Klasse platform improvements).
Industry-standard measurement method for rear legroom is used consistently.
uncertainties: Actual gains depend on platform choice (ICE vs EV packaging) and final interior architecture.

drafts.title: Deliver EV real-world range that meets emerging customer expectations
drafts.description: Customers using the successor EV variant can complete typical daily use and longer trips without frequent charging; real-world driving range matches or exceeds the evolving segment expectation for midsize EVs.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Real-world mixed-cycle range ≥465 km (measured in representative real-world driving tests) for the primary EV variant. In customer trials ≥70% of typical users report they can complete their regular weekly driving without requiring mid-week charging.
assumptions: Battery energy density improvements continue through the late 2020s (e.g., cell pack energy density and packaging improvements sufficient to deliver ≥465 km real-world range in midsize EV packaging).
Acceptable real-world range is measured using a representative mixed urban/highway usage profile and realistic accessory loads.
Charging infrastructure availability will continue to improve but is not assumed to guarantee long-distance comfort without this range.
uncertainties: Final range depends on chosen battery chemistry, vehicle mass, aerodynamics and wheel/tyre selection.
Regulatory or homologation changes could affect how real-world range is declared or measured.

drafts.title: Enable a software‑defined HMI with OTA updates, personalization and a zero‑layer home for top functions
drafts.description: Customers can personalize key HMI shortcuts, receive frequent value-adding OTA improvements, and access major functions from a zero-layer home screen or physical shortcuts so common tasks require minimal interaction.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: OTA reliability: updates delivered to pilot fleet with <0.5% update-related functional regressions. HMI usability: in user testing 90% of drivers can access top 5 commonly used functions (climate, media, nav home, phone, vehicle state) within 2 taps or 1 glance on the home layer.
assumptions: Centralized compute and software-defined architecture are in place for the successor vehicle generation.
OTA regulatory and cybersecurity requirements are satisfied for the target markets at launch.
'Zero-layer' home concepts and personalized shortcuts are accepted patterns by customers when combined with tactile shortcuts for safety-critical controls.
uncertainties: OTA governance and third-party app ecosystems may limit some personalization capabilities initially.
Some markets may require different privacy/consent handling which affects personalization features.

drafts.title: Offer conditional automated driving capability where regulation allows (highway automation up to ~95 km/h)
drafts.description: Customers can use a conditional automated driving mode on supported highways that reduces fatigue on long trips, subject to local regulatory approval and safe-operational limits.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In regulated pilot markets, the feature operates up to 95 km/h and meets applicable conditional-autonomy approval requirements; in customer pilots ≥80% of participants report reduced driving effort and satisfactory behaviour in routine highway scenarios.
assumptions: Regulatory approvals for conditional automated driving (up to ~95 km/h) are available in at least one target market (e.g., Germany) by launch.
Sensor and software maturity is sufficient to meet safety/regulatory requirements for conditional automation at launch.
Acceptance trials and human‑machine interface design will be completed before public release.
uncertainties: Regulatory timelines, market-by-market approvals and liability frameworks may delay deployment.
Required certifications and independent validations could extend roadmap timescales.
